KINDNESS
THANKFULNESS
PERSEVERANCE
"A new command I give you: love one another.
As I have loved you, so you must love one another." John 13:34
Inspired by Jesus’ example, the Trent school community
aims to serve one another in love.
We show kindness to others because God has shown us great kindness.
We live thankful lives, because every good thing comes from God.
We persevere, not giving up, because God is our helper
Welcome from the
Welcome to a glimpse of Trent Primary School, I am very proud to be the headteacher of this very special school.
Life at our school is vibrant and dynamic, filled with diversity and energy. Our curriculum is designed to inspire, challenge, and support each child, helping them discover their strengths and build their aspirations. Every day brings new and exciting opportunities for growth and exploration. Our pupils tell us they love coming to school and enjoy the learning experience, feeling well cared for by staff who truly have time for them. Academic excellence, enriched by our commitment to sport, music, and the arts, and nurtured by our Christian values—this is the essence of life at Trent.
Mrs Chrissy Vassiliou
Headteacher
Upcoming events
School Calendar

Special educational need and disability (SEND)
The Government challenges all schools to be inclusive. By this they mean a welcoming community that seeks to eliminate discriminating attitudes and practice, responds to pupils’ different needs, overcomes barriers to learning and provides suitable learning for all.
It is the aim of the Governors of Trent CE Primary School to try to make our school ‘inclusive’ and welcoming to all.
At Trent CE Primary School, we aim to ensure that all pupils have access to a broad and balanced curriculum and take as full a part as possible in all school activities.
we welcome pupils with Special Educational Needs and make every effort to support them. All our classes are fully inclusive and we have high expectations for all our children, including those with SEN. We provide a differentiated curriculum which caters for the needs of individual pupils. We aim to identify pupils requiring Special Educational Needs (SEN) provision as early as possible. Every child is valued equally and given support according to their needs. By nurturing the whole child and building self-esteem, confidence grows and children acquire the necessary skills to become responsible young people. Working in partnership with parents, all staff encourage children to develop a love of learning, to aspire to achieve their best and support them to succeed.
Our Special Needs Coordinator (SENCo), who does not have a class teaching responsibility, ensures that the needs of SEND pupils are met through co-ordinating support from outside agencies, advising colleagues and monitoring the progress of SEND pupils.
God created all of us in his image. "Imagine how boring the world would be if we were all the same?" At Trent we celebrate diversity, just as God is our helper we strive to help all children to achieve their full potential and model an attitude of kindness so they are in turn are kind to others.
We encourage children to be thankful for the way they and others are created, celebrating successes big and small.
Knowing that God is our helper, gives us the resources to persevere when we find things hard.

Values and Ethos
"A new command I give you: love one another. As I have loved you, so you must love one another." John 13:34
Inspired by Jesus’ example, the Trent school community aims to serve one another in love.
Our school vision is based on Jesus’ words to his disciples before his death and resurrection. He tells them, and us, to keep loving others in the way he has loved. It is this sacrificial love which sits right at the heart of our vision for the Trent School community.
The Parable of the Good Samaritan in Luke 10 perfectly captures for us this pattern of inspiration leading to action. Jesus had been approached by a religious expert who wanted to test Jesus and justify himself. “What must I do to inherit eternal life?” is the timeless question the religious expert asks – but he knows the answer. “Love the Lord your God with all your heart and with all your soul and with all your strength and with all your mind, and Love your neighbour as yourself.” The requirement for eternal life is perfect love.
To illustrate this love, Jesus tells the story of a traveller who is attacked, beaten and left for dead. He is in desperate need but the religious Priest and Levite pass by offering no help. Despite all their religious show, they fell far short of this perfect love. Then an outsider enters the story, a Samaritan man, and incredibly he is the one who cares for the traveller and pays the medical bills out of his own pocket.
Jesus finishes his story by telling the religious expert to go and be like the Good Samaritan. It’s a ‘gulp’ moment. Perfect love is required to receive eternal life, but when we see what perfect love looks like we realise how imperfect our love actually is. So what are we to do?
At Trent we talk about the two possibilities of ‘Law’ and ‘Grace’. We can either try our very best to score the Perfect 10 in loving God and loving our neighbour. We will slave away every day… but we will never quite achieve perfect love. That is the law route.
The grace route, however, begins with Christ. It recognises that we will never love perfectly and so, on our own, we can never inherit eternal life. We are in desperate need of help just like the wounded traveller. In our need, Jesus, the Good Samaritan comes and he binds our wounds and pays the debt we can never pay as he dies on the cross. He loves perfectly on our behalf, and then, as we are inspired by his example, we seek to serve each other in love.
Grace acknowledges that we all fall far short of perfect love, but it never gives up trying to love because we know how much we have been loved by Jesus our Good Samaritan. With this in mind we constantly remind each other how important the start of our vision statement is. It all begins with what Jesus has done for us.

Maths
OUR JOURNEY THROUGH MATHS
Distinctive Christian Character
At Trent, our Maths curriculum is firmly grounded in our Christian vision and values.
It enables pupils to develop a clear understanding of God’s world and to appreciate the beauty, order and logic within His creation. Through Mathematics, pupils are encouraged to persevere when faced with challenge, to show kindness to themselves and others as they learn, and to be thankful for the minds and understanding God has given us. We are thankful that God is a God of order and faithfulness, and that the patterns and principles we discover in maths reflect His dependable nature. As we explore numbers, shapes and relationships, we see evidence of His design and creativity.
Our maths teaching equips pupils with the knowledge, understanding and skills to reason, problem-solve and think logically. These skills help them to make wise decisions, approach challenges with confidence and contribute positively to the world around them.
The curriculum is underpinned by Trent’s core Christian values of kindness, thankfulness and perseverance. These values shape the way pupils learn and interact—encouraging them to support one another, to celebrate progress and to keep going when learning feels hard.
High-quality Maths teaching nurtures curiosity, confidence and resilience. It prepares pupils to use their God-given gifts to serve others and to see that every part of creation, even the order of numbers, points us back to His faithfulness. Through Maths, pupils come to appreciate the wonder of God’s world and their place within it.
Intended Curriculum
At Trent, we have developed a whole-school approach to the teaching of Mathematics that reflects our Christian visionand values. Our curriculum is built around the National Curriculum, with a distinct Trent twist that brings learning tolife through exploration, reasoning and creativity.Mathematics is taught through daily, discrete lessons that give pupils dedicated time to build knowledge andunderstanding.
Cross-curricular links are embedded throughout the wider curriculum so that learning is relevant and
meaningful — for example, using measurement in science, exploring patterns in art or applying number skills in geography.
Each lesson is designed to foster perseverance, curiosity and thankfulness. Pupils are supported to reason, problemsolve and think logically, developing a deep understanding through the Concrete–Pictorial–Abstract approach. This progression enables them to make secure connections and apply their learning with confidence. Maths lessons at Trent are characterised by rich discussion and reflection in a supportive environment. Pupils are encouraged to explain their thinking, listen respectfully to others and approach challenges with determination and kindness. Teachers guide and scaffold learning so that every child can flourish and use their God-given talents to understand His world more deeply.
At Trent, we aim to nurture confident, enthusiastic and life-long learners of Mathematics. Our teaching builds knowledge systematically, encourages curiosity and reflects our belief that perseverance and kindness lead to success. Mathematics is taught through daily, carefully structured lessons that promote fluency, reasoning and problem-solving. Each lesson builds upon prior learning to ensure progression and depth of understanding.
A Concrete–Pictorial–Abstract approach supports all pupils in developing secure conceptual understanding before moving on to more complex ideas. Teachers pay close attention to potential misconceptions and plan opportunities to address these within lessons. Targeted interventions are used flexibly to support pupils who may need additional input, ensuring that every child can make progress. Learning is delivered through a balance of whole-class teaching, small-group work and independent practice, depending on the needs of the learners.
Mental maths is reinforced regularly to strengthen number fluency and confidence. Homework is set to consolidate and extend classroom learning, encouraging children to take ownership of their progress.
Wherever possible, meaningful cross-curricular links are made so pupils can see how mathematics connects with the wider world and God’s creation. Through this approach, our children learn not only how to succeed in maths but also how to appreciate its order, beauty and purpose in everyday life.
Curriculum Delivery
At Trent, each maths lesson has a clear learning objective that pupils understand and can work towards with confidence. Lessons are carefully differentiated to ensure that all children are appropriately challenged and supported.
Assessment is ongoing and draws on a wide range of evidence — including pupil discussions, questioning, observations, practical work, and written responses. These outcomes help teachers build a detailed and evolving picture of each pupil’s understanding, informing future planning and next steps in learning. Termly assessments provide valuable insight into each child’s progress. Data is compared with previous outcomes to identify strengths and any areas requiring further support. Gaps in learning are addressed promptly through targeted interventions, focused class teaching, or additional practice as needed.
At the end of each year, teachers make a summative judgement of attainment based on their professional knowledge of each pupil’s progress across the year. Judgements reflect whether pupils are working towards, meeting, or exceeding the expected learning goals in mathematics. These outcomes form the basis of progress reports shared with parents.
National assessments — including EYFS baseline assessments, statutory testing at the end of Years 2 and 6, and the Year 4 Multiplication Tables Check — provide further evidence of the effectiveness of our maths curriculum. Findings from these are used to review priorities and refine our approach as we continue to strive for excellence in teaching and learning.

Science
OUR JOURNEY THROUGH SCIENCE
Distinctive Christian Character
"A new command I give you: love one another.
As I have loved you, so you must love one
another," (John 13:34).
Inspired by Jesus’ example, the Trent school
serve one another in love.
We show kindness to others because God has
shown us great kindness.
We live thankful lives because every good thing
And we persevere, not giving up, because God is
Science is the study of how God’s world works. Through Biology, we can begin to understand God’s immense power and creativity in making humans, animals, plants in the amazing world that we live in.
Our thankfulness can lead us to understand our responsibility in taking care of the creation entrusted to us.
Our teaching of Physics unlocks the awe and wonder of God’s world and the phenomena within His design, which extends through our incredible solar system. Chemistry enables us to examine the building blocks of how God’s world functions. We develop a thankfulness for the world God has created and the inspirational scientists who have served their communities and through their faith to extend our knowledge, appreciation and development of the world around us. We endeavour to persevere in our own scientific enquiries.
Intended Curriculum
At Trent, we believe that good science education “helps children to make sense of the world around them through investigations and interactions in which they are personally involved.”t Trent, we believe that a good music education allows all children to beconfident, creative and collaborative.
​A high-quality science education provides the foundations for understanding the world through the specific disciplines of biology, chemistry and physics. Science has changed our lives and is vital to the world’s future prosperity, and all pupils should be taught essential aspects of the knowledge, methods, processes and uses of science. Through building up a body of key foundational knowledge and concepts, pupils should be encouraged to recognise the power of rational explanation and develop a sense of excitement and curiosity about natural phenomena. They should be encouraged to understand how science can be used to explain what is occurring, predict how things will behave, and analyse causes.
We aim to ensure that all pupils:
develop scientific knowledge and conceptual understanding through the specific disciplines of biology, chemistry and physics.
develop understanding of the nature, processes and methods of science through different types of science enquiries that help them to answer scientific questions about the world around them.
are equipped with the scientific knowledge required to understand the uses and implications of science, today and for the future.
Curriculum Delivery
Teachers aim for high standards of teaching and learning in school by implementing a curriculum that provides opportunities for children to develop their scientific curiosity and embed their knowledge.
Our lessons are planned according to National Curriculum Programmes of Study (2014) and Understanding the World for EYFS. Our lessons are adapted to take into account individual needs of the pupils in each class in order to extend the learning of all pupils. Science is taught in discrete lessons in order to ensure coverage and understanding.
However, where possible cross-curricular links are made where possible to ensure pupils can recognise the impact of science on other areas of the curriculum.
We ensure that all children are taught with rich learning experiences by:
using our ‘Trent Style’ learning approach that is applied across all subjects.
encouraging scientific questioning though our science big questions
enriching pupil vocabulary by providing children with opportunities to explore key words at home and during lessons.
developing staff CPD through training and using knowledge organisers to support deeper learning for our pupils.
enabling and fostering the children’s natural curiosity by providing children with the opportunity to ask their own questions and carefully planned questioning from teachers.
developing children’s understanding of working as a Scientist through practical and theoretical investigation.
enabling children to reflect on and demonstrate their learning by completing low stakes quizzes.
promoting problem solving, creativity and communication within th classroom through a wide range of enquiries.
regular monitoring of learning to show pupil understanding of concepts and scientific skills.
Fast attaining pupils are further challenged through problem solving or reasoning questions.
Through our intent and implementation of Science, the pupils at Trent Primary School develop a rich and
deep subject knowledge of biology, chemistry and physics. They are able to explore the breadth and
depth of the National Curriculum by the time they complete Year 6 through our coherent and
progressive framework of learning. The children are able to build on their understanding of previous
topics through flashbacks to consolidate and build on prior knowledge and understanding.
Our pupils experience the challenge and enjoyment of learning through carrying out different enquiries
which allow them to not only develop scientific skills, but also to develop and demonstrate their
creativity. Science Week is a time where children area able to develop their skills in Science through
different contexts and apply their learning in unfamiliar contexts.
Science naturally enables and fosters children’s scientific questioning, but at Trent we have enhanced
this through the exploration of ‘Big Questions’. This allows the children to focus their ideas and express
their predictions and understanding of what the answers could be.
We encourage enrichment opportunities beyond the classroom by going on trips, where appropriate, to
give children first-hand experience of Science. Where possible, we promote Science activities at home
for example, competitions and events in science such as Science Week.

Art and Design
OUR JOURNEY THROUGH ART
Distinctive Christian Character
God is creative and made our wonderful world.
God created us to be in His image, and therefore creative too.
We give thanks for the beauty of the world, for the inspiration to create and for the ability to express our thoughts and feelings. Art requires perseverance and patience and we trust in God’s strength when we are challenged. As a school community, we show kindness through encouragement and the celebration of everyone’s unique work.
Intended Curriculum
Art and design is a creative, exciting and inclusive subject for every child. Our curriculum meets the requirements of the National Curriculum while providing a broad and balanced education. Through a cross- curricular approach, we use projects and big questions to drive enquiry-based learning that connects art with wider areas of study. Skills and knowledge are carefully developed across year groups, building on the creativity established in the Early Years Foundation Stage. Art encourages imagination, observation and communication
through the exploration of colour, texture, form and pattern. Pupils also learn about significant artists, craftspeople and designers from a range of times and cultural backgrounds. Ultimately, we aim to prepare children for a media-rich future by helping them form informed and thoughtful cultural opinions.
Our curriculum is aspirational, fostering progressive skills and critical thinking about
art and its role in history and culture. It is creative, encouraging original ideas and innovation, and skill-based, providing opportunities for pupils to explore drawing, painting, sculpture and other techniques. The curriculum is progressive, building on the foundations established in the Early Years Foundation Stage with continuity and development year on year. It is also inclusive, ensuring that all pupils can access learning through appropriate support and differentiation.
A creativity-led, skills-based approach helps develop pupils as inspired and motivated learners. Teaching is hands-on, with opportunities to work independently, in pairs or in groups, both inside and outside the classroom. Pupils gain experience in painting, drawing, sculpture, digital artwork and photography, with each lesson focused on specific skills and linked to the wider curriculum project. In Key Stage 2, pupils use sketchbooks for practice and reflection, while in Key Stage 1 they explore skills in varied formats and sizes. Pupils study artists and designers, examining artistic movements and their historical contexts, and they respond through discussion, writing and their own creative work. Prior learning is regularly revisited to strengthen progression and deepen understanding across year groups.
Curriculum Delivery
Impact
The impact of our art and design curriculum is seen in lessons that have clear objectives for skill development, while also allowing space for creativity beyond set outcomes. Teaching is inclusive and differentiated to ensure engagement and challenge for all pupils. Assessment is ongoing and draws on discussions, questioning and teacher observations to provide a full picture of each pupil’s progress and creativity.

Intended Curriculum
In line with the National Curriculum (2014), Trent ensures high-quality computing education that
fosters computational thinking and creativity. Computing is taught discretely, with cross-curricularlinks to subjects like maths, science, art and design, and design and technology where relevant. This approach allows for step-by-step skill development and addresses misconceptions. By highlightingcomputing’s relevance across subjects, we nurture invention, resourcefulness, and readiness for life in modern Britain.
At Trent, pupils build a strong foundation in computer science, including abstraction, logic,
algorithms, and data representation. They learn to break down problems and create programs using tools like Scratch, FMS Logo, and Crumble. Physical computing is taught across the school—from Beebots in EYFS and KS1 to micro:bits in KS2—to deepen their understanding of programming.
At Trent Primary School, we value computational thinking as essential for problem-solving, system design, and understanding human-machine intelligence. Pupils develop logical reasoning, pattern recognition, abstraction, and evaluation skills, becoming creative and critical thinkers who collaborate effectively. Through computing, they learn to find, share, and assess information while gaining a critical understanding of computers, software, the internet, and their impact on society.
At Trent, computing is taught through discrete lessons and embedded across the curriculum. Based on the National Curriculum (2014), our computing curriculum is structured around five strands: Online Safety, Programming, Data and Information, Creating Media, and Computing Systems and Networks. This ensures comprehensive coverage and deepens both declarative and procedural knowledge. Topic links help pupils see the relevance of computing in real life, and staff receive training to stay updated with developments in the subject.
Each computing lesson at Trent reinforces prior learning, introduces new vocabulary, and uses
enquiry-led mini-questions to support pupils in applying subject-specific terminology.

At Trent, we believe that a good music education allows all children to beconfident, creative and collaborative.
We have established a school curriculum plan for music which is:
Aspirational. Pupils are given opportunities to excel in the progressive and increasingly challenging objectives of each unit.
Logical, broad and balanced. Pupils experience music from throughout history and from around the world, as well as performing on instruments such as keyboards, ukuleles, samba drums and mixed percussion.

At Trent, the study of music involves engaging pupils in lessons that enable them to understand and access increasingly complex musical ideas and skills through a focus on practical music making. Doing this through a breadth of topics allows pupils to experience wide ranging musical traditions, and develop skills in a range of instruments, voice and technology.
Curriculum Delivery
At Trent, we implement a practical approach to learning and teaching in music that develops our pupils as young musicians. Through lessons centred on performance and composition, our pupils develop understanding of musical vocabulary, analysis, notation and historical and geographical context alongside performance and composition skills.
Our lessons are planned according to National Curriculum Programmes of Study (2014). Our lessons are adapted to take into account individual needs of the pupils in each class in order to extend the learning of all pupils. We ensure that all children are taught with rich learning experiences by:
using our ‘Trent Style’ learning approach that is applied across all subjects.
structuring each scheme of work so that it culminates in the completion of a performance or composition (which is always shared with the class, and often also in Class Assemblies).
ensuring that the focus remains on the key practical objectives to help make learning activities engaging. Skills in theory and listening are developed alongside practical tasks.

Through our intent and implementation of music, the pupils at Trent Primary School develop a rich and deep subject knowledge. As they move up the school, they continually build on their knowledge and skills, which they begin to draw upon to create cohesive performances and compositions.
Our pupils experience the challenge and enjoyment of learning through performing and composing on a variety of instruments and in a range of styles. They enjoy working towards creating recordings or perfecting performances which are then shown in their Class Assemblies.
Through learning theory and listening skills alongside practical ones, pupils understand and appreciate their real-world relevance. Their increasing theoretical skills then support their performances (e.g. being able to follow notation to help when learning a new song).
Pupils enjoy taking part in performances outside the classroom. Throughout their time at Trent, they have the opportunity to work towards a number of performances during music lessons, including class assemblies, the Nativity, the End of Year Show, and the Barnet Infant and Junior Music Festivals. Pupils also have the opportunity to become part of the choir, which sings at the School Fairs, CAMEO dinners at Church House, as well as Young Voices at the 02 and Prom Praise for Schools at the Royal Albert Hall. A number of pupils also have lessons at school on instruments including the piano, drums, guitar, violin, flute, clarinet and saxophone. These pupils enjoy sharing their performances in assemblies.

Curriculum overview
OUR CURRICULUM
Distinctive Christian Character
The Trent Curriculum enables children to immerse themselves in exciting, meaningful, and memorable learning experiences.
At Trent, we see Christ as our ultimate inspiration (John 13:34). We believe that every human being is made in God’s image and therefore has infinite worth. This belief underpins our curriculum and our commitment to helping each child flourish as a unique individual.
Intended Curriculum
The Trent Curriculum is designed to be ambitious, coherent and inclusive. We intend that every pupil, across every year group and subject, gains deep foundational knowledge, develops powerful disciplinary skills, and grows as a well-rounded individual.
We place curriculum coherence and progression at the heart of our planning, ensuring that pupils’ learning in one year builds efficiently into the next. Key “big ideas” and recurring themes—such as inspiration, service, identity and resilience—run through and link subjects, providing meaning and continuity. Through careful sequencing and purposeful bridging of concepts, pupils revisit and build on prior knowledge, allowing them to make connections, deepen understanding and apply learning in new contexts.
We expect that all learners—including those with special educational needs or from less advantaged backgrounds—will be challenged to deepen understanding and extend thinking.
Moreover, we believe education is about more than knowledge: our curriculum is shaped to foster character, personal development, ethics, well-being, curiosity, leadership and global citizenship.
Inspirational people, past and present, from all cultures and backgrounds, are studied across the curriculum. We draw out the good in every life we explore, recognising that no one but Jesus is perfect; by learning from others, we learn more about the wonderful, diverse world that God has made.
Curriculum Delivery
To deliver on our intent, the Trent Curriculum uses a combination of discrete knowledge sessions and contextualised, skills-based learning, chosen deliberately for each subject and year.
Lessons are carefully planned with modelling, retrieval practice, scaffolding and deliberate practice, enabling pupils to master and revisit core concepts.
Subject leaders ensure that the progression of disciplinary skills—such as scientific method, historical enquiry and problem solving in mathematics—is explicit and consistent across year groups.
Formative and summative assessment are embedded within each unit to check pupils’ understanding, identify misconceptions and inform responsive teaching. Tracking of curriculum goals and pupil outcomes enables ongoing reflection, adjustment and refinement.
Professional development and curriculum review cycles are integrated so that teachers continually evolve their practice based on evidence and pupil data.
Our broader school life—collective worship, displays, extra-curricular activities, trips and workshops— reinforces and extends curriculum learning, giving pupils authentic opportunities to apply, present and celebrate their learning.
The curriculum is celebrated through the totality of Trent’s life: class assemblies, exhibitions, community events and a daily rhythm of engaging activities. This broad and balanced curriculum enables children to discover new interests, develop strengths and advance passions and talents.
‘Big questions’ engage children and encourage independent, creative thinking across subject areas, while the key themes of inspiration and service flow throughout all we do.
We judge the success of the Trent Curriculum through three key lenses:
Pupil outcomes and mastery – pupils know more, remember more and can apply their learning in new ways. Across key assessments, transitions and internal checks, we expect continuous progress for all.
Pupil voice and reflection – pupils can articulate what they have learned, make connections,
reflect on their progress and plan next steps.
Wider development and habits – beyond academic measures, pupils grow in character, confidence, curiosity, service-mindedness, resilience, ethical reasoning and cultural awareness.
We systematically evaluate curriculum effectiveness through termly reviews, feedback cycles and analysis of outcome data, using this evidence to refine our curriculum continually. Subject leaders hold responsibility for evaluating how well curriculum design is translating into pupil learning and experience, ensuring that the Trent Curriculum continues to inspire, challenge and nurture every child.

Design and Technology
OUR JOURNEY THROUGH DT
Distinctive Christian Character
God created and designed the
God has a good design
We give thanks to God for providing us with the beauty and order of creation, which
inspires us to design with purpose and imagination. We also thank God for giving us the ability to solve problems and to use our creativity to serve others.
Design and Technology requires perseverance and patience. We trust in God’s strength and help when we face challenges.
As a school community we show kindness to ourselves and to others through encouragement and celebration of our design work. All design is unique and we celebrate individuality and expression, as well as the creativity of designers throughout time and across the world.
Intended Curriculum
Design and Technology at Trent is practical, engaging and inclusive, equipping children to solve problems, think critically and create with purpose. We aim for children to become resourceful, innovative and capable designers and makers, to understand the design, make, evaluate cycle, and to gain technical knowledge and skills. Pupils also learn to evaluate how design impacts daily life, culture and history, and to use the language of Design and Technology confidently, preparing them to thrive in a technological world.
Our curriculum is aspirational, with skills and knowledge developing progressively across year groups. It is global, incorporating influential designers and the cultural and historical context of their work, and creative, encouraging innovation and risk-taking. The curriculum is skill-based, allowing pupils to apply technical knowledge to real projects with safe practice, and purposeful, with work critiqued and refined continuously. Learning is progressive, building on foundations established in the Early Years, and inclusive, ensuring accessibility for all pupils through appropriate support and differentiation.
Curriculum Delivery
Our approach is creativity-led and skills-based, with learning that is hands-on and provides opportunities to work independently and collaboratively. Lessons follow the design, make, evaluate cycle and are linked to wider projects, while technical knowledge is taught through meaningful and engaging contexts. Cooking and nutrition are taught practically, alongside an understanding of healthy diets. Pupils study designers, innovators and scientists, analysing the problems they solved and the impact of their work. Vocabulary is taught in context, displayed in classrooms and revisited regularly, and skills and knowledge build year on year, with prior learning continually reinforced.
The impact of our Design and Technology curriculum is evident in lessons with clear objectives for skill development, while also allowing space for creativity beyond set outcomes. Teaching is inclusive and differentiated to ensure engagement and challenge for all pupils. Assessment draws on class discussions and questioning, observations of practical work, and evaluation of designs and projects. At the end of each year, teachers make a holistic judgement on whether pupils have met, exceeded or are working towards expectations, and these outcomes are used to report progress to parents.
